ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=30^\circ$, $AC=12$, $\sin B=\frac{3}{5}$, find the length of $BC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $AD\perp BC$ at point A, with D as the foot\\
In $\triangle ADC$, $AC=12$, $\angle C=30^\circ$\\
$\therefore AD=\frac{1}{2}AC=6$, $CD=\sqrt{3}AD=6\sqrt{3}$\\
In $\triangle ABD$, $\sin B=\frac{3}{5}$\\
$\therefore AB=10$\\
$\therefore BD=8$\\
$\therefore BC=BD+CD=8+6\sqrt{3}$\\
$\therefore$ The length of $BC$ is $\boxed{8+6\sqrt{3}}$

method.method_draft: Use the Law of Sines and an angle-sum identity. From the image, read that ∠B is acute, so sin B = 3/5 implies cos B = 4/5 rather than −4/5. From the text, AC = 12 is the side opposite ∠B, and ∠C = 30°. By the Law of Sines, AC/sin B = BC/sin A, so 12/(3/5) = BC/sin A, giving common ratio 20. Since A = 180° − B − C, sin A = sin(B + C). Thus sin A = sin(B + 30°) = sinB cos30° + cosB sin30° = (3/5)(√3/2) + (4/5)(1/2) = (3√3 + 4)/10. Therefore BC = 20·(3√3 + 4)/10 = 8 + 6√3.
